newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain coal industry to cut 7,000 jobs before 2005.
newsitem.headline: Spain coal industry to cut 7,000 jobs before 2005.

text.p: Spanish Industry Minister Josep Pique signed an agreement with trade unions for the coal mining industry on Tuesday which forecasts cuts of around 30 percent in the workforce and declining public funding in the next seven years.
The plan, considered positive by unions, predicts 7,000 jobs out of the current 24,400 will be lost and foresees progressive cuts in public aid which was 150 billion pesetas in 1997.

"This plan ...covers the necessary restructuring of the mining sector while meeting European Union requirements and reducing taxpayers costs of sustaining the sector," said Pique at a press conference following the signing.
Domestic coal costs double the average international coal, Secretary of State for Energy Nemesio Fernandez-Cuesta said.
"At present domestic coal is the source of 25 to 30 percent of energy used in the country. This percentage is set to fall to around 15 percent," Fernandez-Cuesta said.
"In recent years the sector has lost a lot of jobs, around half in the last seven to eight years," Pique said.
The plan forecast a reduction in public aid of six percent in 1998, and then a cut of four percent each year until 2005.
"With this pact we put an end to the trend seen in recent years of increasing aid to the sector," Cuesta said.
In the plan, production of Spanish domestic coal is set to fall around 30 percent, with a fall of 28.32 percent from 1997 to 2005 in guaranteed consumption.
That means that Spanish energy firms are guaranteeing to use around 18 million tonnes this year, with this amount declining to 13 million tonnes in 2005, according to the plan.
Spain is a net importer of cheaper international coal.
The pact forecasts also an increase of public investment in those areas where mining provided the bulk of economic activity, Pique added.
